clauses.label: Section 1.
clauses.text:
Section 1. Policy. Every person should be treated with respect and dignity 
and should be able to live without fear, no matter who they are or whom 
they love. Children should be able to learn without worrying about whether 
they will be denied access to the restroom, the locker room, or school 
sports. Adults should be able to earn a living and pursue a vocation knowing 
that they will not be fired, demoted, or mistreated because of whom they 
go home to or because how they dress does not conform to sex-based 
stereotypes. People should be able to access healthcare and secure a roof 
over their heads without being subjected to sex discrimination. All persons 
should receive equal treatment under the law, no matter their gender identity 
or sexual orientation. 
These principles are reflected in the Constitution, which promises equal 
protection of the laws. These principles are also enshrined in our Nation’s 
anti-discrimination laws, among them Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 
1964, as amended (42 U.S.C. 2000e et seq.). In Bostock v. Clayton County, 
590 U.S.l(2020), the Supreme Court held that Title VII’s prohibition on 
discrimination ‘‘because of . . . sex’’ covers discrimination on the basis 
of gender identity and sexual orientation. Under Bostock’s reasoning, laws 
that prohibit sex discrimination—including Title IX of the Education Amend-
ments of 1972, as amended (20 U.S.C. 1681 et seq.), the Fair Housing 
Act, as amended (42 U.S.C. 3601 et seq.), and section 412 of the Immigration 
and Nationality Act, as amended (8 U.S.C. 1522), along with their respective 
implementing regulations—prohibit discrimination on the basis of gender 
identity or sexual orientation, so long as the laws do not contain sufficient 
indications to the contrary. 
Discrimination on the basis of gender identity or sexual orientation manifests 
differently for different individuals, and it often overlaps with other forms 
of prohibited discrimination, including discrimination on the basis of race 
or disability. For example, transgender Black Americans face unconscionably 
high levels of workplace discrimination, homelessness, and violence, includ-
ing fatal violence. 
It is the policy of my Administration to prevent and combat discrimination 
on the basis of gender identity or sexual orientation, and to fully enforce 
Title VII and other laws that prohibit discrimination on the basis of gender 
identity or sexual orientation. It is also the policy of my Administration 
to address overlapping forms of discrimination.

clauses.label: Sec. 2.
clauses.text:
Sec. 2. Enforcing Prohibitions on Sex Discrimination on the Basis of Gender 
Identity or Sexual Orientation. (a) The head of each agency shall, as soon 
as practicable and in consultation with the Attorney General, as appropriate, 
review all existing orders, regulations, guidance documents, policies, pro-
grams, or other agency actions (‘‘agency actions’’) that:

clauses.label: (i)
clauses.text:
(i) were promulgated or are administered by the agency under Title VII 
or any other statute or regulation that prohibits sex discrimination, includ-
ing any that relate to the agency’s own compliance with such statutes 
or regulations; and

applicable law.

to impair or otherwise affect:

relating to budgetary, administrative, or legislative proposals.

(b) This order shall be implemented consistent with applicable law and 
subject to the availability of appropriations.

defects.source_says: EO 14168 sec. 7(b) (90 FR 8615): '...including but not limited to Executive Orders 13988 of January 20, 2021, 14004 of January 25, 2021, 14020 and 14021 of March 8, 2021, and 14075 of June 15, 2022. These Executive Orders are hereby rescinded' (an express whole-order rescission of EO 13988 dated 2025-01-20)

evidence_checked: held original text and SOURCES.jsonl row (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run)
record.reasoning: Every quoted span in the claim was re-hashed and matched byte-for-byte at its char offsets against the held text files (text_sha256 equal). The original's SOURCES.jsonl row in jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run has the same sha256, URL and page_or_item (confidence high); the PDF blob itself is not held, a custody gap the coordinator is fixing, not by itself a ground for rejection. Number, date and title agree with jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv and the held FR text (the WPA 1944 list does not reach these orders). Section 2 of EO 14148 (90 FR 8237, signed 2025-01-20, held text EO_14148.txt) lists this order by number, date and title among actions 'hereby revoked', with no later effective date and no saving clause; section 3(b) leaves past actions to DPC/NEC review, which supports the transferred_or_accrued savings statement. A cruden number search of held order texts was run (/tmp/claude-0/review-k01-EO_N.json) and every hit was read; no instrument earlier than 2025-01-20 ends any clause. The end dates are wrong and contradict the claim itself: whole_order_end and every clause's first_end give 2022-01-20, but the cited actor EO 14148 was signed 2025-01-20, and every reason in the claim says 2025-01-20. A 2022 end is also impossible on the record, since no held instrument of that date names this order (held citations are only EO 14035, 14075 and 14091, all non-ending, then EO 14148 and 14168). Second defect: Section 7(b) of EO 14168 (held text EO_14168.txt, right after the quoted span ending at char 11087) continues: 'These Executive Orders are hereby rescinded, and the White House Gender Policy Council established by Executive Order 14020 is dissolved.' So EO 14168 expressly rescinds this order as a whole on 2025-01-20. The claim's source note says it supersedes only conflicting provisions and 'does not revoke this order as a whole', which misstates the source, and the quote is cut off just before the rescinding sentence. The end date is unaffected because the two orders bear the same date, but the stated reason for a concurrent ending instrument is wrong. The inventory (14 clauses, sec. 1 through 4(c)) is complete. The correct end would be 2025-01-20 by EO 14148 sec. 2(d), with EO 14168 sec. 7(b) as a concurrent express rescission.

versions.research_rationale:
Identity: the held registered text of Executive Order 13988 is the official Federal Register text layer at 86 FR 7023, PDF pages 1-3 (Federal Register / Vol. 86, No. 14 / Monday, January 25, 2021); it names Executive Order 13988 of January 20, 2021, Preventing and Combating Discrimination on the Basis of Gender Identity or Sexual Orientation, and runs from the title to the signature block. The complete clause inventory was checked against the numbered section headings of that text. Section 2(d) of Executive Order 14148 of January 20, 2025 (Initial Rescissions of Harmful Executive Orders and Actions, 90 FR 8237, Federal Register of January 28, 2025) lists Executive Order 13988 of January 20, 2021 among the executive actions that section 2 declares hereby revoked. The held text of Executive Order 14148 states no effective date later than its signing, so the revocation operates from its signing date, 2025-01-20. Whole-order revocation by name is the first end of every clause that had not already been exhausted by performance. The order has no other ending instrument before 2025-01-20 in the packet's later-event chain, which for this order lists besides Executive Order 14148: Executive Order 14168. Each such instrument is recorded in the source notes with its date and why it is not an earlier end; none reinstates this order. The packet's name search of held order texts for this order's number returned, among texts dated on or after 2025-01-20, only Executive Order 14148 and Executive Order 14168. The later-source search is recorded by the three machine searches selected on the sheet: the U.S. Code release point 119-121 (edition current through 2026-10-09), the eCFR point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14 with the CFR bulk files, and the Federal Register executive-order disposition catalog; their coverage statements were read and each is marked complete. Savings are addressed in the savings statement. The first end of the whole order is 2025-01-20.

savings_residuals.reason: Section 3(b) of Executive Order 14148 directs the Director of the Domestic Policy Council and the Director of the National Economic Council to review all Federal Government actions taken pursuant to the orders, memoranda and proclamations listed in section 2 and to take necessary steps to rescind, replace or amend such actions as appropriate. Because rescission of actions already taken is left to later action, Federal actions already taken under Executive Order 13988 before 2025-01-20 were not themselves revoked by section 2 and stood until rescinded, replaced or amended individually. No held source identifies a particular surviving action or its later fate, so none is asserted.
